Synopsis: Alfira has seen her friends, people she considered family, dragged screaming into the nigh. She is upset and only just holding it together. She asks the player to save the prisoners in Moonrise. She believes any survivors were taken to Moonrise Towers and urgently asks the player to go rescue the prisoners. retrieved_synopses: Alfira has just watched friends she treated like family get ambushed and dragged off by Absolute cultists; she’s grieving and barely holding herself together, describing gruesome mutilations and saying Rolan somehow managed to save some of them. She believes any survivors were taken to Moonrise Towers and urgently asks the player to go rescue the prisoners. Off‑screen, Moonrise is run by zealous, sadistic Absolute guards who enjoy tormenting prisoners, routinely use telepathic mind‑melds to check for tadpoles/allegiance, and can detain, humiliate, or report people on a whim. Prior contacts with tower sentries, events on the roof/audience/execution path, or whether the player is recognized as a tadpole bearer will affect how easily the player can gain entry or how hostile the guards will be.

The player is confronted by some Bhaalist cutlists who've just murdered a civilian in Bloomridge park. The cultists recognise the player as even greater targets - those Orin wants dead. They turn hostile, with more appearing after the dialogue, leaving the player outnumbered.

In this scene, Alfira arrives unannounced at the player's camp. Depending on the grove, she either 1) asks the player if she can join their camp 2) be mad at the player for upsetting her in the grove and ask to spend the night (she got lost and needs shelter) or 3) if the player has missed the grove will ask the player to come help her friends the tieflings.In all instances, when the player and Alfira go to sleep, the player will awaken to find blood on their hands and Alfira's dead body next to her. They will have killed Alfira in their sleep. This is a scene specific to the Dark Urge custom origin.

A drow commander leading an attack on a group of tiefling refugees. She is following the orders of a new god, the Absolute, and is zealous and sadistic. In this situation, the player has sided with her and betrayed the tieflings - a fact she enjoys a great deal.

Minthara, now freed from the influence of the Absolute and from a jail cell at Moonrise Towers, joins the players' party at their Camp. She is shaken from her experiences, and is coming to terms with the fact that she now understands the truth about the Absolute - that it is not a god at all, but something monstrous that lies within Moonrise.She wishes to join with the party, knowing they can help her get vengeance against the cult, and knowing that they are her only hope of salvation, thanks to the Prism that they hold, which shuts out the Absolute's voice.
context: Alfira has just watched people she considered family ambushed by Absolute cultists and dragged off screaming; she’s grieving, barely holding herself together, and describes gruesome mutilations (eyes, tongues) while blaming a possible traitor. She says Rolan managed to save some people and that he stayed behind in the grove because of the player. Alfira urgently asks the player to go to Moonrise Towers — she believes any survivors were taken there and fears the worst. Off‑screen, Moonrise is run by zealous, sadistic Absolute guards who enjoy tormenting prisoners and routinely use telepathic mind‑melds to check for tadpoles or allegiance; prior contacts with sentries or whether the player is known to bear a tadpole will affect how easily they can gain entry or how hostile the guards will be.
